blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — edoxaban NVAF renal-function limitation
stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation has a new prescription for edoxaban. The calculated creatinine clearance is 108 mL/min. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Administer edoxaban as prescribed because higher creatinine clearance improves edoxaban exposure and makes stroke-prevention efficacy more reliable than at lower clearance values.
options.B: Question the prescription because SAVAYSA should not be used for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation when CrCl is greater than 95 mL/min; another anticoagulant should be considered.
options.C: Request a 50% edoxaban dose reduction because creatinine clearance above 95 mL/min is managed by lowering the dose rather than selecting a different anticoagulant.
options.D: Recommend stopping anticoagulation entirely because a creatinine clearance above 95 mL/min makes anticoagulant therapy unsafe regardless of which agent is selected.

rationale: Current SAVAYSA labeling contains a boxed limitation for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation: edoxaban should not be used when creatinine clearance is greater than 95 mL/min because ischemic stroke occurred more often than with warfarin in this subgroup, and another anticoagulant should be used. The label directs assessment of CrCl before initiation. Therefore B is correct. A reverses the efficacy relationship, C invents a dose-reduction strategy that applies instead to impaired renal function, and D incorrectly generalizes the edoxaban-specific limitation to all anticoagulant therapy.
educational_objective: Identify the edoxaban NVAF limitation in clients with CrCl greater than 95 mL/min and question the prescription so an alternative anticoagulant can be considered.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: DailyMed updated July 10, 2025; prescribing information revised October 2023; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Boxed Warning; Indications and Usage §1.1; Dosage and Administration §2.1; Warnings and Precautions §5.1: assess CrCl before therapy; do not use SAVAYSA for NVAF when CrCl >95 mL/min because of increased ischemic stroke risk versus warfarin; another anticoagulant should be used.
source_claim_supported: For NVAF, edoxaban should not be used when CrCl exceeds 95 mL/min because efficacy is reduced and ischemic stroke risk was higher versus warfarin; another anticoagulant should be used.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review pertinent laboratory data; identify contraindications and medication-specific precautions; administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete renal-function management decisions without absolute-word distractor cues.
Balanced option lengths and preserved the NVAF-specific nature of the >95 mL/min limitation without generalizing it to anticoagulation overall.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B uniquely matches the boxed SAVAYSA limitation for NVAF. The answer is not length-cued, and the item does not misstate the restriction as a general contraindication to anticoagulation.
